name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3431
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: Start leaving spots on arch, without regard for the consequences

indicators.note: the start of the next word leaves it, so its opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: freckles are small brown spots on the skin
arch means knowing and sly, as in an arch smile

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for a spot beneath an arch, careless of what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: FRECKLES loses its F, and SLY is placed on the end to give RECKLESSLY. 'Arch' is the adjective meaning roguish, not the curved structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting recklessly means acting rashly, heedless of what may result.

clue.text: Magical spinner in rear trains is inclined to go over family

blocks.note: the rump is the hindquarters
els are elevated railways, as in Chicago's El
something that tilts is inclined
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A trick top rides in the back of a train sloping above a family.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'to go over' means one piece sits above the next. An El is an American elevated railway, like Chicago's.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpelstiltskin is the fairy-tale imp who spins straw into gold.

clue.text: Solid shapes: covering for an old Roman wagon

blocks.note: cones are solid geometric shapes
the toga was the robe of an ancient Roman citizen

explanation.surface: Geometry blocks are draped over an ancient cart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conestoga was the heavy covered wagon used by American pioneers heading west.

clue.text: Glowing and innocent one, dispatched without a bit of sarcasm

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the word for dispatched loses a letter
a bit of signals taking only one letter of the following word to remove

blocks.note: a lamb is the image of innocence
dispatched means sent
the first letter of sarcasm

explanation.surface: A radiant and guileless person is sent off without a hint of sneering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent one' reads as describing a person, but the lamb is the proverbial emblem of innocence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that flickers or glows softly.

clue.text: Pet spaniel usually licks kids' faces

indicators.note: a face is the front of something, so the front letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A household dog tends to lick children's faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like the dog, but it is the noun for a fit of pique.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pet is to be in a sulk, a bad mood of sullen resentment.

clue.text: Varnished billboard leaving out first broadcast

indicators.note: leaving out first means dropping the opening letter of the word for a billboard
broadcast means put out on the air, so it is the spoken form that counts

blocks.note: a placard is a poster or sign; without its first letter it is said like the answer

explanation.surface: A polished advertising hoarding is left out of the first broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: PLACARD minus P leaves LACARD, which said aloud matches LACQUERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a hard glossy coating, so a lacquered surface has been coated like varnish.

clue.text: Recalled relative with island bird

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the word for a relative is read backwards

blocks.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island
sib is short for sibling, a brother or sister

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a family member who lived on an island with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Sib, short for sibling, is common in American crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill.

clue.text: Solution from a Google cofounder and the head of eBay

indicators.note: the head is the top, so just the opening letter of the company name is used

blocks.note: Sergey Brin co-founded Google with Larry Page
the first letter of eBay

explanation.surface: A tech fix comes from a Google founder and eBay's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' looks like an answer to a problem but means a liquid mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Brine is a solution of salt in water.

clue.text: Sandpile produces all the elements for an Italian item on a tourist's bucket list?

definitions.text: an Italian item on a tourist's bucket list?

blocks.note: surface reading: a heap of sand supplies the raw materials, as if for building something

blocks.clueFragment: an Italian item on a tourist's bucket list?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the eight different letters of the word sandpile are every letter the answer phrase uses, and the phrase is a famous saying about a southern Italian city

explanation.walkthrough: SEE NAPLES AND DIE repeats letters, but its distinct letters are exactly S, A, N, D, P, I, L, E, so 'sandpile' holds all its elements without being a strict anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says one should view that Italian city before dying, so it is literally a bucket-list item for travellers.

clue.text: UC's map might represent one!

indicators.note: to represent can mean to present again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A University of California map would show a university's grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: UC is the University of California, whose map would naturally show a campus, so the whole clue is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds and buildings of a university, exactly what a UC site map depicts.

clue.text: A couple of minutes with headless beast? That's barely sufficient

indicators.note: a couple means two, so only the opening pair of letters of the next word is kept
without a head, the word for a beast loses its first letter

blocks.note: the first two letters of minutes
a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: A short spell with a decapitated creature, and someone remarks that it barely does the job.
explanation.walkthrough: MI plus ANIMAL without its A gives MINIMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minimal is the smallest amount possible, only just enough.

clue.text: Cold, sentient computer rocks a vessel

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
HAL 9000 is the self-aware computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey
rocks is slang for ice, as in a drink served on the rocks

explanation.surface: A chilly, thinking machine shakes a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning ice cubes in a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a goblet, especially the cup used for wine at Communion.

clue.text: Holiday in one direction (not north)

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for the compass point that follows

blocks.note: eastern means lying in or toward the east, one of the compass directions
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A vacation spent travelling one way, avoiding the north.
explanation.walkthrough: EASTERN with its N removed leaves EASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection, a public holiday in many countries.

clue.text: Summon to replace a writer? Not applicable

blocks.note: to sub is to substitute for someone
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
N/A is the usual abbreviation for not applicable on a form

explanation.surface: An editor calls someone in to stand in for an author, then decides that option does not apply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summon' and 'replace' read as one instruction, but they are the definition and the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To subpoena someone is to order them by writ to appear in court, a formal summons.

clue.text: Right at home in places — except for a place to drink and watch the game

definitions.text: a place to drink and watch the game

indicators.note: being at home in a place means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
spots are places or locations
bar means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: Someone feels at home anywhere except in the one venue that shows the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Except for' sounds like a qualifier, but it supplies the second word, as in 'all bar one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports bar is a pub with screens showing live games to drinkers.

clue.text: Dentures discounted because they stick out?

definitions.text: Dentures discounted because they stick out?

blocks.note: surface reading: false teeth sold off cheaply in a sale
setter's reading: teeth costing a single dollar, which also names front teeth that protrude

explanation.walkthrough: A buck is a dollar, so cheap teeth are teeth for a buck; the phrase also names prominent upper teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes protruding front teeth, an overbite of the upper incisors.

clue.text: Coils backward into a bobbin

indicators.note: going backward means the word is read from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: coils are loops of rope or wire

explanation.surface: Thread winds the wrong way onto a sewing reel.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOPS read in reverse gives SPOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is a cylinder on which thread or wire is wound, much like a bobbin.

clue.text: What you might find in a pit or casket: God

definitions.text: What you might find in a pit

blocks.note: taken as written
a casket is a small chest or box
Ra is the ancient Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A grim list of things buried in a hole or a coffin, ending with the divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like part of the definition but supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra pit is the sunken area in front of a stage where the musicians play.

clue.text: Pallid, reflective, and penetrating — that is, thunderstruck

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the word for pallid is turned round
penetrating means getting inside, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: wan means pale and sickly
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: A pale, thoughtful, sharp-witted person is left speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' looks like thoughtful, and 'penetrating' like sharp; both are instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in awe means feeling overwhelming wonder, the state of someone stunned or astonished.

clue.text: Extraterrestrial certainly keeps back pastry

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the run of letters sits within the words before it
back means the held letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An alien is sure to be holding onto a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'terrestRIAL CErtainly'; reading it backwards gives ECLAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger of choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Attachments to some pants: scales, fins, etc.

blocks.note: first meaning: pouches fastened to the front of old-fashioned breeches
second meaning: bits of a particular fish

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word into a fish name plus the word for portions.
explanation.definitionFit: Codpieces were flaps on Renaissance hose, and literally the word also reads as portions of a cod.

clue.text: Lizards disturbed us again

indicators.note: things disturbed are thrown out of their order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Reptiles have bothered the speakers one more time.
explanation.definitionFit: Iguanas are large tropical American lizards.

clue.text: Organize prohibition behind schedule

blocks.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, a ban
late means running behind time

explanation.surface: An administrator sorts out a ban that is running late.
explanation.walkthrough: TABU is the less common spelling of taboo.
explanation.definitionFit: To tabulate is to arrange data in a table, putting it in order.

clue.text: Company that makes medicines for a hound?

blocks.note: first meaning: the German pharmaceutical firm famous for aspirin
second meaning: a hound howls, so it is one who bays

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: a creature that bays.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayer is the German drugmaker known for aspirin, and a baying hound is jokingly a bayer.

clue.text: Youth seen around ancient city with a bowl

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for a youth wraps the city

blocks.note: a teen is a young person
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A young tourist is spotted at an archaeological site holding a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the Sumerian city of Abraham, is the setter's favourite ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A tureen is a deep lidded dish for serving soup.

clue.text: Woman's energy: what carries essential information for the next generation

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

blocks.clueFragment: what carries essential information for the next generation
blocks.note: DNA carries the genetic code passed from parent to offspring

explanation.surface: A woman's vitality is described as what she passes on to her children.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the name to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Fruit in the bottom of a boat, I'm told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the answer matches the spoken words

blocks.clueFragment: the bottom of a boat, I'm
blocks.note: a keel runs along the bottom of a boat, followed by I'm said straight

explanation.surface: Someone reports finding a piece of fruit lying in the hull of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm' does double duty: part of the sound and part of the indicator. Said quickly, keel-I'm runs together into the name of the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The key lime is a small, tart Florida citrus fruit, famous in key lime pie.

clue.text: Gave money to put on a talk show?

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on
taken as written
TED is the conference series famous for its short filmed talks

explanation.surface: Someone paid to stage a chat show on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk show' suggests a television programme, but it points to TED talks.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give money to a cause, so donated means gave money.

clue.text: Reno confused a fiery classical musician?

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters of the city name are jumbled

blocks.note: the Nevada city, taken as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Nevada city baffles a fiery player of old music.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the Roman emperor fiddled while Rome burned, hence a fiery classical musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero, emperor of ancient Rome, supposedly played music during the great fire, a classical-era fiddler.

clue.text: Someone unlikely to have 27 piles originally keeps interrupting Blanchett

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the word that follows it
interrupting means breaking into, so these letters go inside the actress's name

blocks.note: piles are heaps
the first letter of keeps
Cate Blanchett, the Australian actress

explanation.surface: A miser hoarding money keeps butting in on Cate Blanchett.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to the answer at 27 across, DONATED, so the definition is a person unlikely to give.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person, hardly someone to have given money to charity.
